notes: The 15 'Visual Arts' units are Grade 3-4 geography and history (globe, continents, states of India, early humans, agriculture, trade), not art: a global 'art'->'Visual arts' replacement in the source also corrupted words ('PVisual artsicipation', 'EVisual artsh', 'bVisual artser'); they are mapped by their text to World Around Us rows, and the school's actual visual-arts programme is absent from the unit map except the Memory Drawing and Doodle & Describe routines.

NCF preparatory PE rows carry both nested standards, LS-1 (CG-3..6) and LS-2 (CG-1..2), which repeat each other almost verbatim and are mapped identically; LS-2's own CG-3 (mental engagement, C-3.1/3.2) collided with LS-1's CG-3 id and is missing from ncf_competencies.json.

NCERT has no art or HPE outcomes below Class 9, so every preparatory and middle competency has an empty ncert list; 25 Class 9-10 art outcomes (care of materials and instruments, self-confidence, teamwork values, artists' lives, planning-to-performance) state what NCF-SE places in the middle stage and are mapped to those middle C rows, which therefore carry Class 9-10 evidence.

Vocational education has no preparatory rows and no NCERT outcomes; Primary Computing G3-4 units on algorithms, loops, debugging and data-driven problem solving map to ncf.math.P.CG-4 (the only NCF row naming computational thinking, no C fits), while networks, hardware, AI and data-handling units get no competency because NCF preparatory mathematics has no data-handling row.

Champak (Hindi reading) is mapped to R2 preparatory rows on the assumption that English is R1 at the school; if Hindi is R3 there is no preparatory R3 row to use. G1-2 bands of computing and routines use foundational domain rows (excluded from the graded lists as instructed), so mixed-band units carry one foundational and one preparatory target.
